raw_response:
I am 53 years old and I have farmed this land since I was 18. I only finished primary school, but I know my fields from doing the work every year. I have 6 mu total. I plant wheat and maize on 4 mu, and I keep 2 mu for stevia. The stevia I planted last spring — it is a perennial crop, so this year it will grow back from the roots. I covered the stevia roots with straw last winter so the frost would not kill them. Hebei winters are cold.

For my winter wheat: I sowed it last October on 4 mu. I used Jinmai 22, it is an improved variety. My neighbor Lao Wang used it and got good yield last year, so I switched from my old seed. Last autumn I rotary tilled the field and put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer. Now in spring, when the wheat turns green, I will topdress with 40 jin of urea per mu at the jointing stage. That is 20 kilograms of urea. I figure the nitrogen: 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer at 16% nitrogen gives 6.4 kilograms of nitrogen. The urea at 46% nitrogen gives 9.2 kilograms. So total nitrogen is about 15.6 kilograms per mu. Phosphorus and potassium come only from the compound fertilizer, so 6.4 kilograms each per mu. I will irrigate three times this spring and early summer: once when the wheat turns green in March, once at jointing in April, and once during grain filling in May. Each time I pump from my well. Diesel for the pump costs about 30 yuan each time. I spray pesticide twice: once for weeds with herbicide, and once for aphids. I expect 450 kilograms per mu this year. Last year I got less because of dry weather, but this year I will irrigate on time.

For summer maize: Right after I cut the wheat in early June, I sow maize on the same 4 mu. There is no time to plough deeply — I just open rows and plant directly. I use Zhengdan 958, it is a hybrid seed. I buy it from the seed dealer in town. At planting, I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the planting holes. Then when the maize reaches the big trumpet stage, I topdress with 40 jin of urea per mu. That gives the same as the wheat: about 15.6 kilograms of nitrogen per mu, 6.4 kilograms of phosphorus, and 6.4 kilograms of potassium. I irrigate twice: once when it is tasseling in July, and once when the grain is filling in August. If the summer rain is heavy, maybe I skip one, but usually I need both. I spray twice for armyworm and weeds. I expect 500 kilograms per mu. Last year I got 480, so I hope for a bit more.

For stevia: My 2 mu of stevia is my cash crop. In spring, when the soil warms up, I rotary till between the rows to loosen the soil. I put 60 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a base. The stevia grows back from the roots in April. When it reaches about 20 centimeters, I cut it for the first harvest in June. After the first cut, I put 20 jin of urea per mu so it grows back fast. I get a second cut in August, and I put another 20 jin of urea after that. If the weather stays warm, I get a small third cut in September. So total urea is 40 jin per mu, which is 20 kilograms. The compound gives 4.8 kilograms of nitrogen, and the urea gives 9.2 kilograms. Total nitrogen is 14 kilograms per mu. Phosphorus and potassium are 4.8 kilograms each from the compound. I irrigate four times over the season because stevia likes moisture. I only spray pesticide once, because stevia does not have many bugs, maybe some caterpillars. I dry the leaves in the yard and the buyer comes to the village to collect them. Last year I got 140 kilograms dry leaves per mu. This year I want 150 kilograms per mu if the weather helps.

I think about money carefully. Fertilizer is expensive now. One bag of urea is 120 yuan, compound fertilizer is 150 yuan per bag. For 6 mu, I need many bags. But if I cut back on fertilizer, the yield drops, and I lose more money than I save. A bad harvest means I cannot help my son with his expenses or pay my own medical costs. So I would rather put a little too much than too little. I watch my neighbors. Most people in my village put similar amounts. If everyone puts 40 jin of urea on wheat, I do the same. I don't want to try something strange and fail. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends money home, which helps me buy inputs. But I still calculate every yuan. Change is risky. Last year's practice is my starting point.
